subject: english
question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

By the way a lorry / crashed into the car but / the boys were lucky and / escaped with only minor injuries.
solution:
The correct answer is '**By the way a lorry**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The segment "**By the way a lorry**" incorrectly introduces an event without proper punctuation or contextual relevance for the phrase "**By the way**."
 
• Removing "**By the way**" corrects the contextual flow and focuses directly on the main event, improving clarity.
 
• The lack of punctuation (specifically, a comma after "**By the way**") renders the introduction awkward and grammatically incorrect.
 
• Ensuring the introductory phrase directly relates to the critical information improves the readability and coherence of the narrative.

Therefore, the correct answer is ‘**Option 3**’.

 

**Correct Sentence**: ***A lorry** crashed into the car, but the boys were lucky and escaped with only minor injuries.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1) "**crashed into the car but**" is correctly structured to convey the central action and its immediate aftermath, connecting two clauses in a way that properly uses "but" to contrast outcomes.
 
• Option 2) "**escaped with only minor injuries**" effectively communicates the outcome of the incident, implying the seriousness could have been greater but wasn't, due to luck or other factors.
 
• Option 4) "**the boys were lucky and**" provides necessary context about the boys' fate following the crash. It underscores their fortune in an otherwise potentially dire situation, contributing vital information to the narrative.
